name: MAX3051EKA+T
title: MAX3051: +3.3 V, 1 Mbps, low-supply-current CAN transceiver, SO-8 and SOT23-8
summary: A CAN bus transceiver that runs from one +3.3 V supply and links a CAN controller's TXD and RXD to the two bus wires, CANH and CANL. The RS pin picks one of three modes: high speed up to 1 Mbps, slope control with the edge rate set by a resistor for up to 500 kbps, or a low-current standby; SHDN adds a shutdown below 1 µA. The bus pins tolerate -7 V to +12 V of common mode and carry ±12 kV HBM ESD protection, current limiting and thermal shutdown. It comes in 8-pin SO and SOT23 for -40 °C to +85 °C.
key_figures: up to 1 Mbps (high speed); up to 500 kbps (slope control)
35 mA typ dominant, 2 mA typ recessive

notes: The + marks a lead-free, RoHS-compliant package; a trailing T is tape and reel.

pins.name: TXD
pins.function: Data to send, from the CAN controller; CMOS/TTL levels. Pulled up inside by about 75 kΩ, so an open TXD keeps the bus recessive.

pins.name: VCC
pins.function: +3.3 V supply. Decouple to GND with 0.1 µF.

pins.name: RXD
pins.function: Received data, to the CAN controller; CMOS/TTL levels. Low while the bus is dominant.

pins.name: SHDN
pins.function: Shutdown, CMOS/TTL levels. High puts the part in shutdown; an internal 75 kΩ pulldown holds it in normal operation when open.

pins.name: CANL
pins.function: Low line of the CAN bus.

pins.name: CANH
pins.function: High line of the CAN bus.

pins.name: RS
pins.function: Mode select. Low or grounded: high-speed mode. A resistor to GND: slope-control mode, its value setting the output slew rate. High: standby.

circuits.title: Typical operating circuit
circuits.description: The MAX3051 between a CAN controller and the bus. The controller's TX0 drives TXD and RXD returns to its RX0; both share the VCC rail, which has 0.1 µF to ground at the transceiver. A resistor of 25 kΩ to 200 kΩ from RS to ground selects slope-control mode and sets the edge rate. Two 120 Ω resistors sit across CANH and CANL. SHDN is left open, which is normal operation.

circuits.title: Several receivers on one CAN bus
circuits.description: One twisted pair runs from the MAX3051 to a far transceiver, with a 120 Ω resistor across the pair at each end. Two more transceivers tap the pair along its length on stubs, which are kept as short as possible.
notes: U1's VCC, GND, RS and SHDN are not part of this circuit.

equations.name: Slope-control resistor

where.RRS: resistor from RS to GND, kΩ

equations.note: Slope-control mode covers roughly 40 kbps to 500 kbps.

equations.name: Receiver decision
equations.expr: VDIFF = VCANH - VCANL; RXD low when VDIFF > 0.75 V, high when VDIFF < 0.75 V

operation.text: A CAN physical-layer transceiver for a single +3.3 V rail. It turns the controller's TXD into a differential drive on CANH and CANL and turns the bus difference back into RXD. It is aimed at non-automotive systems that do not need the full ISO 11898 fault protection. Built on a BiCMOS process.
The bus inputs work from -7 V to +12 V of common mode, wider than the -2 V to +7 V that ISO 11898 asks for.
TXD low drives the bus dominant (CANH high, CANL low). TXD high or open leaves it recessive, with each line held near VCC/2 through 5 kΩ to 25 kΩ.

A comparator looks at CANH minus CANL against an internal +0.75 V threshold: above it RXD is low, below it RXD is high. RXD always reflects the data on the bus. If CANH and CANL are shorted together, or terminated and left undriven, RXD is high.
RS grounded (below 0.3 x VCC) gives the fastest edges and data rates up to 1 Mbps. The bus cable in this mode is shielded twisted pair, against EMI.

A resistor from RS to GND (RS held between 0.4 x VCC and 0.6 x VCC) limits the slew rate of CANH and CANL, for data rates up to 500 kbps. The slower edges cut EMI and let the bus run on unshielded twisted or parallel wire. The resistor value follows from the equation for RRS and the slew rate against RRS curve.

RS above 0.75 x VCC switches the transmitter off and puts the receiver in a slow, low-current state; supply current drops to about 8 µA. A dominant bit on the bus pulls RXD low, and the controller is expected to answer by putting the transceiver back in normal operation. On entering standby RXD stays high for up to 4 µs whatever the bus does; after that it goes low only while the bus is dominant. tSBRXDL is measured with the bus dominant.

SHDN high turns both transmitter and receiver off, leaving CANH and CANL unconnected and supply current under 1 µA. SHDN low or open is normal operation. From shutdown the part needs at least 20 µs to reach standby.

CANH and CANL limit their short-circuit current. Above a junction temperature of +160 °C the part turns off: the bus lines go recessive and every function stops. It comes back once the die cools by about 25 °C, to near 135 °C. ESD protection is ±12 kV, Human Body Model.

A multidrop bus is one pair of wires running directly from node to node, never a star, terminated with 120 Ω at each of its two ends. Any branch off that pair is a stub; on a stub the fast edges of the data reflect back along the bus and reduce the noise margin, which can corrupt data. Stubs are kept as short as possible, above all in high-speed mode; slope-control mode tolerates them better, though short stubs still help. The slew-rate limit of slope-control mode also lowers EMI and reflections from cable that is not terminated correctly.
The part has no layout needs beyond usual practice. VCC is bypassed to GND by a 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor placed close to the package, with short leads and wide traces.
